text: I think the biggest change has been in how I deal with stress around my health. I have endometriosis, and for years the pain and the uncertainty have been a constant source of stress: will I be able to go to work, will I have to cancel plans again, will the next surgery help. I used to feel betrayed by my body and furious at the doctors who didn't take me seriously. During the experience I felt a profound tenderness for my body, like it was a wounded animal that needed care rather than punishment. I've carried that feeling with me. When I have a flare now, I still get frustrated, but I try to respond with care: heat pad, rest, gentle movement, cancelling plans without guilt. I've also found an online community of people with endometriosis, which has been a huge support. It's made the stress so much more bearable, and I've stopped fighting with myself on top of fighting the illness.

Ich habe gelernt, dass ich bei Stress nicht immer sofort eine Lösung finden muss. Manchmal hilft es, einfach abzuwarten und die Situation zu beobachten. Früher habe ich in Panik irgendetwas getan, nur um das Gefühl der Hilflosigkeit loszuwerden. Heute kann ich die Unsicherheit besser aushalten.

I'm less of a worrier now. I used to spend hours imagining everything that could go wrong, at work, with my kids, with money. During the experience I saw how much of my life I'd been wasting on worry, and how rarely the things I worried about actually happened. Now when I catch myself worrying, I ask if there's anything I can actually do right now. If there is, I do it. If not, I try to let it go. It doesn't always work, but my stress levels have gone down a lot and I'm sleeping better.
Calmer under pressure. I handled my wedding planning without a single meltdown, which my mum says is a miracle.

Ich habe die Erfahrung in einer Zeit gemacht, in der ich mit einer schweren Erschöpfungsdepression zu kämpfen hatte. Ich war seit Monaten krankgeschrieben und hatte das Gefühl, dass ich nie wieder arbeiten kann. Jede kleine Belastung, wie ein Telefonat mit der Krankenkasse oder ein Arzttermin, hat mich völlig überfordert. In der Erfahrung habe ich gespürt, wie viel Kraft eigentlich noch in mir steckt, nur verschüttet unter Erschöpfung und Selbstzweifeln. Ich habe auch gesehen, wie sehr ich mich über Jahre hinweg überfordert habe, weil ich niemanden enttäuschen wollte. Diese Erkenntnis war schmerzhaft, aber auch befreiend. In den Monaten danach habe ich mit meiner Therapeutin daran gearbeitet, meine Grenzen besser wahrzunehmen. Heute arbeite ich wieder, allerdings in Teilzeit, und ich gehe mit Stress viel achtsamer um. Ich merke früher, wenn es zu viel wird, und kann dann rechtzeitig gegensteuern, z.B. indem ich mir einen freien Tag nehme oder Aufgaben abgebe.

The experience showed me that I've been using sarcasm and humour to avoid dealing with stressful things. Whenever something bad happened, I'd make a joke and move on, and the feelings would just pile up. Now I try to actually feel things before I joke about them. It's harder, but I don't get these random breakdowns anymore where everything I've been ignoring comes out at once.

I've become better at handling stress because I've learned to ask for what I need. I used to suffer in silence and expect people to read my mind, and then I'd be resentful when they didn't. During the experience I saw how unfair that was, to them and to me. Now I'm more direct. When I'm overwhelmed at home, I tell my husband I need him to take over dinner. When work gets too much, I tell my manager. It feels vulnerable, but it works.

Ich nehme belastende Situationen heute gelassener hin. Ich weiß, dass ich nicht alles kontrollieren kann, und versuche, mich auf das zu konzentrieren, was in meiner Macht steht. Das hat mir in den letzten Jahren sehr geholfen, besonders bei der Pflege meiner Mutter.

I'm transgender and I came out about a year after the experience. The months around coming out were the most stressful of my life: telling my family, my employer, dealing with the medical system, facing people's reactions. I genuinely don't think I could have done it without the experience. During the trip, I saw myself as I really am, and I felt so much love and acceptance for that person. It was like meeting myself for the first time. That gave me the courage to come out, and it also gave me a kind of inner stability that has helped me through all the stress since. When people misgender me or say hurtful things, it still hurts, but it doesn't shake my sense of who I am. I know who I am now. I've also found a wonderful community of other trans people who support each other, and I lean on them when things get hard. My parents took some time, but they're coming around.

I'm better at letting go of things I can't change and focusing on what I can do. It has really reduced my stress levels at work and at home, especially with the endless home renovation we've been doing.

Ich habe durch die Erfahrung gelernt, auf meinen Körper zu hören. Früher habe ich Stress immer ignoriert, bis ich krank wurde. Jetzt merke ich früher, wenn ich angespannt bin, z.B. an Verspannungen im Nacken oder an Schlafproblemen. Dann nehme ich mir bewusst Zeit für Entspannung, gehe in die Sauna oder mache einen langen Spaziergang. Das hilft mir, nicht wieder in eine Überlastung zu rutschen.
I'm much less bothered by things. I used to get really stressed about my job but now I just do it and go home.

Before the experience, I would describe myself as a chronically stressed person. I'm a lawyer, I have three kids, and I've always been the type to say yes to everything and then panic. I was constantly running late, constantly behind, constantly apologising. The experience was at a retreat that my sister booked for me as a birthday present, because she was worried about me. I didn't expect much. But in the experience, I saw myself running on a hamster wheel, faster and faster, and I saw my kids standing outside the wheel, waiting for me to come out and play. It broke my heart. Since then, I've made some big changes. I've cut back my hours, I've stopped volunteering for every committee, I've hired someone to help with the house. More importantly, I've stopped seeing stress as a sign of how important I am. When things get busy, I remind myself of that image, and I ask myself whether this is worth missing my kids for. Usually it isn't. I'm much calmer now, and my kids say I'm more fun.

Ich bin in Konflikten ruhiger geworden und kann besser zuhören. Früher habe ich mich sofort angegriffen gefühlt und bin laut geworden. Heute versuche ich zu verstehen, was mein Gegenüber eigentlich will, und das entschärft viele Situationen.

I'm better at stopping my anxiety from spiralling. I used to have one anxious thought and then twenty more would follow, until I was in a full panic. During the experience I watched my thoughts like a chain reaction and saw how each one triggered the next. Since then I try to catch the first one and gently set it aside. I also use a breathing technique I learned in the integration sessions afterwards.

Not much has changed in how I deal with stress. I'm still quite anxious, and I still procrastinate when things get hard. The experience was beautiful, but I don't think it had a lasting effect on that part of my life. Maybe I need to work on it in other ways.

Ich habe während der Erfahrung sehr deutlich gesehen, wie sehr ich mich in meinem Leben von Angst habe leiten lassen. Ich habe einen sicheren Beruf gewählt, den ich nicht mag, ich bin in einer Stadt geblieben, in der ich mich nicht wohlfühle, und ich habe mich nie getraut, meine Meinung zu sagen. In der Erfahrung habe ich gespürt, wie viel Leben ich dadurch verpasst habe, und ich habe auch gespürt, dass ich den Mut habe, etwas zu ändern. Seitdem habe ich einiges verändert. Ich habe eine Weiterbildung angefangen, um mich beruflich neu zu orientieren, und ich plane, im nächsten Jahr umzuziehen. Diese Veränderungen sind natürlich auch mit Stress verbunden, aber es ist ein anderer Stress. Es ist der Stress von jemandem, der sein Leben selbst gestaltet, nicht der Stress von jemandem, der sich ständig vor allem fürchtet. Mit belastenden Situationen gehe ich heute mutiger um. Ich gehe Probleme an, statt sie zu vermeiden, und ich vertraue darauf, dass ich Lösungen finden werde.
I'm less reactive and more reflective now. When something stressful happens I take time to think about how I want to respond. My relationships have benefited a lot from that.

I've become much better at handling the stress of my job as a social worker. I work with families in crisis, and I used to take everything home with me. I couldn't sleep, I'd think about the kids I work with constantly, and I was on the edge of burnout. During the experience I felt a sense of being part of something larger, like I'm one small part of a big web of people trying to help. I'm not responsible for saving everyone. That has made a big difference. I still care deeply, but I can leave work at work.
Ich mache mir weniger Sorgen und schlafe besser, auch wenn es stressig ist. Das ist für mich eine große Veränderung.

The experience helped me deal with the stress of my father's long illness and death. He had dementia for six years, and I was his main carer for the last two. It was the hardest thing I've ever done. I was exhausted, angry, guilty, and grieving all at once. The experience happened about halfway through. During it, I felt my father's love for me very strongly, the father he was before the illness. I also felt that the illness was not him, and that underneath everything he was still there. That helped me so much. I was able to be more patient with him, to find moments of connection even when he didn't know who I was, and to forgive myself when I lost my temper. When he died, I was sad, but I also felt at peace. I knew I had done my best. I also learned to accept help during that time, from my siblings, from a carers' support group and from a respite service, which I had refused before.
I've learned to set limits and say no. That alone has made my life a lot less stressful, and I'm not exhausted all the time anymore.

Seit der Erfahrung bin ich gelassener im Umgang mit meinen Kindern. Ich habe zwei Teenager, und es gibt oft Streit. Früher habe ich mich sehr schnell aufgeregt und bin laut geworden. Heute kann ich eher durchatmen und versuchen zu verstehen, was in ihnen vorgeht. Ich erinnere mich daran, wie ich selbst in dem Alter war. Das hilft mir, ruhig zu bleiben.
I'm more grounded and less easily thrown off by unexpected events. I trust myself to figure things out.

I would describe my experience as a kind of reset for my nervous system. I grew up in a war zone and came to this country as a teenager. I've always been hypervigilant, every loud noise, every raised voice, every police car would send me into a state of panic. I learned to live with it, but it was exhausting. I took part in a clinical trial with psilocybin for PTSD, and the experience was very hard at times. I relived some things I had never talked about. But I also felt, for the first time in my life, completely safe. It's hard to describe how strange and wonderful that was. Since then, my reactions to stress have changed. I still startle at loud noises, but I recover much faster. I can tell myself that I'm safe now, and my body believes me more often. I've also started talking to my family about what we went through, which we never did before, and that has brought us closer.

Ich bin seitdem achtsamer mit mir selbst. Ich merke früher, wenn mich etwas belastet, und kann darauf reagieren, bevor es zu viel wird. Ich nehme mir regelmäßig Zeit für mich, um zur Ruhe zu kommen, z.B. durch Meditation oder einen Spaziergang im Wald. Das hilft mir sehr.

I'm much more able to accept that life is uncertain and that I can't control everything. That was always my biggest stressor. Now when something unexpected happens, like when my flight was cancelled and I was stuck in an airport for two days, I can roll with it. I even ended up having a nice time exploring the city. A few years ago I would have been in tears.
I don't think it changed how I handle stress much, to be honest. Life has been pretty calm, and when it isn't I do what I always did.

Die Erfahrung hat meinen Umgang mit Stress grundlegend verändert. Ich war vorher ein Mensch, der Probleme immer mit sich selbst ausgemacht hat. Ich habe niemandem von meinen Sorgen erzählt, weil ich niemandem zur Last fallen wollte. Das hat dazu geführt, dass ich mich oft sehr allein gefühlt habe, besonders in schwierigen Zeiten. In der Erfahrung habe ich eine tiefe Verbundenheit mit anderen Menschen gespürt. Ich habe gesehen, dass wir alle miteinander verbunden sind und dass es ein Geschenk ist, anderen helfen zu dürfen. Seitdem traue ich mich, anderen von meinen Problemen zu erzählen und um Hilfe zu bitten. Als ich letztes Jahr meinen Job verloren habe, habe ich meinen Freunden sofort davon erzählt, und sie haben mir sehr geholfen, mit Kontakten, mit Zuspruch und einfach damit, dass sie da waren. Ich habe auch gemerkt, dass sie froh waren, dass ich mich ihnen anvertraut habe. Heute habe ich einen neuen Job und fühle mich in meinem Freundeskreis viel mehr zu Hause.
I'm better at recognising my limits and pacing myself when life gets busy, so I don't crash.

Since the experience I've become much better at dealing with my anger. I used to explode when I was stressed, and I said a lot of things I regretted to my wife and kids. During the experience I saw my anger as a scared little boy shouting to be heard. That changed something. When I feel the anger rising now, I try to listen to what that little boy needs. Usually it's rest, or reassurance, or just to say that I'm overwhelmed. My family says I'm much calmer, and I haven't had a real blow-up in over a year.
Ich habe gelernt, dass ich nicht perfekt sein muss. Das hat mir viel Stress genommen, sowohl im Beruf als auch im Privatleben.

The experience helped me cope with a very stressful period in my life when I was going through infertility treatment, and then a high-risk pregnancy. I've always been an anxious person, and the uncertainty of it all was nearly unbearable. During the experience, which was about a year before we started treatment, I had a vision of a child, and I felt a deep sense of trust that whatever happened, I would be okay. I held on to that during the treatment, and especially during the pregnancy, when there were several scares and I spent weeks on bed rest. I still had moments of panic, of course, but I always came back to that sense of trust. My partner and I also leaned on each other a lot, and on a few close friends who had been through similar things. Our daughter was born healthy last spring. Looking back, I'm amazed at how I coped. I think the old me would have completely fallen apart.
I'm less stressed by other people's opinions of me. I used to worry so much about what everyone thought. Now I care less, in a healthy way, and that has taken a lot of pressure off.

Ich bin nach der Erfahrung zunächst sehr unruhig gewesen und hatte Schwierigkeiten, mit Stress umzugehen. Alles war mir zu viel, und ich hatte manchmal Panikattacken. Mit der Zeit hat sich das gelegt, und ich habe gelernt, mit diesen Gefühlen umzugehen. Ich habe mit Atemübungen und Sport angefangen. Heute würde ich sagen, dass ich besser mit Stress umgehen kann als vor der Erfahrung, aber der Weg dahin war nicht einfach.
Less dramatic about things. I see that most problems are smaller than they seem in the moment.

I'm a police officer, and the job comes with a lot of stress and trauma. For years I dealt with it the way many of my colleagues do, by drinking, joking, and never talking about it. I was getting more and more irritable and isolated, and my marriage was suffering. A colleague who had been through a psilocybin retreat for first responders suggested I try it. The experience was intense. A lot of things came up that I'd buried, a child I couldn't save, a shooting I was involved in, the time I nearly died in a car chase. I cried more than I have in my whole adult life. Since then I've been dealing with stress very differently. I talk about what I see at work with my wife and with a therapist. I've cut back on drinking a lot. I go to the gym and I've started fishing again, which I used to love. I'm much calmer, and my marriage is better than it's been in years. I've also become a kind of informal peer supporter for younger officers.
Ich bin weniger ängstlich, wenn es um meine Gesundheit geht. Früher habe ich bei jedem Symptom das Schlimmste befürchtet, heute kann ich gelassener bleiben und abwarten.

I think the main thing is that I've learned to separate the event from my story about it. When something stressful happens, there's the thing itself, and then there's everything my mind adds: this always happens to me, I'm such an idiot, this will ruin everything. During the experience I could see that difference really clearly. Now I try to deal with the thing itself and drop the story, and stressful events feel much more manageable.
I'm more okay with failure and setbacks. They feel like part of life now, not catastrophes.

Ich habe die Erfahrung gemacht, als ich mitten in einer Krise steckte. Ich war Anfang dreißig, hatte gerade mein Studium abgebrochen, war von meinem Freund verlassen worden und hatte das Gefühl, dass mein Leben ein einziges Scheitern ist. Ich hatte Angst vor jeder Entscheidung und habe mich wochenlang in meiner Wohnung verkrochen. In der Erfahrung habe ich eine unglaubliche Weite erlebt, als würde ich über einer Landschaft schweben und mein ganzes Leben von oben sehen. Ich habe gesehen, dass mein Leben noch lang ist, dass es viele Wege gibt und dass ich nicht gescheitert bin, sondern einfach an einer Kreuzung stehe. Das hat mir unglaublich viel Mut gegeben. In den Monaten danach habe ich eine Ausbildung zur Ergotherapeutin angefangen, die mir sehr viel Freude macht. Ich habe auch gelernt, mit schwierigen Situationen anders umzugehen. Ich sehe sie heute eher als Teil einer größeren Reise und nicht mehr als Beweis dafür, dass ich nichts tauge.
I'm less reactive and more patient with myself and with others. Small problems don't get to me anymore.

I've stopped trying to numb my stress. Before the experience I smoked weed every evening to wind down, and I thought it helped. During the experience I saw that the weed was just covering up a lot of anxiety and sadness that never got dealt with. I quit a few weeks later. It was rough at first, I was more anxious and couldn't sleep well. But now, a year later, I deal with stress much better. I exercise, I talk to my girlfriend, and I let myself feel things. I'm less foggy and I actually solve problems instead of avoiding them.
Ich bin entspannter geworden, gerade wenn es im Job hektisch wird. Ich lasse mich nicht mehr so schnell mitreißen und kann meinen eigenen Rhythmus besser halten.

Since the experience I have a deeper sense of meaning in my life, and that helps me deal with stress. I used to feel like my life was just a series of tasks and obligations, and every stressful thing felt pointless and exhausting. During the experience I felt connected to something larger, and I saw that my small life is part of a bigger story. That has given me a kind of resilience. When things are hard, I remind myself that it's part of the journey and that it matters.
